newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 7.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- China protested against the landing by a Japanese nationalist legislator on the disputed Diaoyu Islands. A Hong Kong group burned Japanese flags and said it was determined to land on the islands to demonstrate Chinese sovereignty.
-- SING TAO DAILY -- Post-handover leader Tung Chee-hwa said the future Special Administrative Region government would not allow activities which advocate Taiwan and Tibet independence.

-- APPLE DAILY -- China has a list of top members of triads, or organised criminal gangs, in Macau who were also involved in crime on the mainland and was considering giving it to police in the Portuguese-run enclave to help them combat a crime wave.
-- WEN WEI PO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin gave a speech urging all Chinese on the mainland to study the Basic Law, Beijing's mini-constitution for post-handover Hong Kong.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Tung's office has made detailed decisions on the transfer of the Land Fund to the post-handover government. After the handover on July 1, the fund will become an independently operated part of foreign currency fund.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Speculation of a change in contol at Sing Tao Holdings sent shares in the loss-making publishing group more than 11 percent higher as reports suggested chairman Sally Aw and her family might be poised to sell their 68 percent stake.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- A senior U.S. congressman revealed that efforts in Congress to delay or limit the renewal of Most Favoured Nation trade status for China were being abandoned.
-- China's Gezhouba Co Ltd, the company building the Three Gorges dam, the world's largest hydroelectric project, will offer shares on Thursday in Shanghai to raise 1.1 billion yuan.
